items.prompt: What is a habitat?

options.why: Food is something a habitat gives an animal. A habitat is a place.

options.text: the place where a plant or animal lives

options.why: A baby animal is called its young.
Weather is rain, sun or wind. A habitat is a place.

hints: A habitat is a kind of home.
Think about where a fish or a camel lives.
Ask: is a pond a food, a place or a type of weather?
items.explanation: A habitat is the place where a plant or animal lives. It gives the living thing food, water and shelter.

items.prompt: Match each animal to its habitat.

figure.alt: Five animals: a camel, a polar bear, a fish, a monkey and a crab.

hints: Think about where you have seen each animal on TV or in books.
Match the ones you are sure about first.
Start with the camel. Is its home hot and sandy or cold and icy?
items.explanation: Camels live in deserts, polar bears in the icy Arctic, fish in ponds, monkeys in rainforests and crabs on the seashore.

items.prompt: Pond or desert? Sort the living things.

figure.alt: A pond habitat and a desert habitat.

hints: A pond is wet. A desert is very dry.
Ask: does this living thing need lots of water around it?
Start with the tadpole. Can it live out of water?
items.explanation: Frogs, ducks and tadpoles live in or near ponds. Camels, cactuses and desert lizards are suited to the hot, dry desert.

items.prompt: Which animal is best suited to a hot, dry desert?

options.why: A polar bear has thick fur for icy places. It would get too hot.
A whale needs to live in the sea.
A frog needs damp places and water for its eggs.

hints: Think about which animal can go a long time without water.
Which animal has wide feet for walking on sand?
Ask: which animal is often shown in pictures of sand dunes?
items.explanation: A camel is suited to the desert. It can go a long time without drinking, and its wide feet do not sink in the sand.

items.prompt: Choose all the ways a camel is suited to the desert.

figure.alt: A camel walking in a sandy desert.

options.text: wide feet that do not sink in sand
long eyelashes to keep sand out
can go a long time without drinking
thick white fur for the snow
options.why: Deserts are hot and sandy. Thick white fur suits polar bears in the snow.
Camels breathe air with lungs. Gills are for fish.

hints: Think about what is hard about living in a desert.
Deserts are hot, sandy and dry.
Start with the wide feet. How would they help on soft sand?
items.explanation: Wide feet stop a camel sinking in sand, long eyelashes keep sand out of its eyes and it can go a long time without water.

items.prompt: What does a camel store in its hump?

options.why: Many people think so, but the hump stores fat.
Sand stays outside the camel.
Camels breathe air into their lungs. The hump is fat.

hints: Many people get this one wrong.
The camel uses what is in the hump when food is hard to find.
Ask: what store helps an animal when there is little food?
items.explanation: A camel's hump stores fat. The camel can use this fat when there is little food in the desert.

items.prompt: A polar bear has thick ___ to keep it warm.

figure.alt: A polar bear in the icy Arctic.

hints: Look at what covers the polar bear's body.
It is white and soft, like a warm coat.
Think about what keeps a cat warm.
items.explanation: A polar bear has thick fur and a layer of fat under its skin. They keep it warm in the icy Arctic.

items.prompt: Why do fish not need to come up for air?

options.text: They hold their breath all day.
options.why: Fish breathe all the time, using their gills.
Fins help fish swim. Gills help them breathe.

options.text: They breathe with gills under water.

options.why: Fish do need air. Their gills take in air that is mixed into the water.

hints: Look at the sides of a fish's head.
Fish have special body parts for breathing in water.
Ask: which body part takes air from the water?
items.explanation: Fish breathe with gills. Gills take in the air that is mixed into the water, so fish can stay under water.

items.prompt: Where would you find each animal? Sort the cards.
hints: Some small animals like damp, dark places.
Other animals need branches to climb, rest or nest.
Start with the worm. Does it like dark, damp soil?
items.explanation: Worms, woodlice and centipedes like the damp, dark places under logs and stones. Birds, monkeys and owls live up in trees.

items.prompt: Choose all the animals you might find in a flooded rice field.

figure.alt: A flooded rice field with shallow water.

options.why: Camels live in dry deserts.
Polar bears live in the icy Arctic.

hints: A rice field is warm, wet and muddy.
Think about animals that like shallow water.
Start with the frogs. Do they like wet places?
items.explanation: Frogs, ducks and snails all live in flooded rice fields. The shallow, warm water gives them food and shelter.

items.prompt: An owl hunts at night. Which feature helps it most?

options.why: Webbed feet help ducks swim.
A hump helps a camel in the desert.
Gills help fish breathe in water.

options.text: big eyes for seeing in dim light

hints: Night is dark. What is hard about hunting then?
Think about which sense the owl needs most at night.
Look at the owl's face. What is very big?
items.explanation: An owl has big eyes that help it see in dim light. It also has very good hearing to find animals in the dark.

items.prompt: A cactus lives in the desert. How is it suited to living there?

figure.alt: A cactus with a thick stem and spines.

options.text: It stores water in its thick stem.

options.why: Big thin leaves would lose water quickly. A cactus has spines.
Deserts get very little rain.
Deserts have very little water.

hints: Think about how the cactus keeps water for dry days.
Look at the thickest part of the cactus.
items.explanation: A cactus stores water in its thick stem. Its spines lose very little water and keep thirsty animals away.

items.prompt: Polar bears and penguins can both live in icy places. Which is true?

figure.alt: A polar bear, a penguin and the Earth.

options.text: They live together near the North Pole.
options.why: Penguins live in the south of the world, so wild penguins and polar bears never meet.

options.text: Polar bears live in the north and most penguins live in the south.
Both of them live in hot deserts.
options.why: Both are suited to cold water and ice.

options.text: Penguins are a kind of bear.
options.why: Penguins are birds. They have feathers and lay eggs.

hints: Think about the top and the bottom of a globe.
Polar bears live in the Arctic. Is that in the north or the south?
Ask: do you ever see polar bears and penguins in the same wild place?
items.explanation: Polar bears live in the Arctic, near the North Pole. Most penguins live in the far south, near Antarctica. They never meet in the wild.

items.prompt: Look at the food chain. What would happen to the birds if all the caterpillars disappeared?

figure.alt: Food chain: a leaf is eaten by a caterpillar, and the caterpillar is eaten by a bird.

options.why: The birds eat caterpillars, so they would have less food.
The birds need the caterpillars for food.
With no caterpillars eating them, there might be more leaves.

hints: Follow the arrows. Who eats whom?
The arrow points from the food to the animal that eats it.
Ask: what does the bird eat in this chain?
items.explanation: In this food chain the birds eat caterpillars. Without caterpillars, the birds would have less food and would need to find other food.

items.prompt: Orangutans live in rainforests in Sumatra and Borneo. Why do they need the forest?

figure.alt: An orangutan in a rainforest tree.

options.why: Rainforests are warm and wet, with no snow.

options.text: They need the sea to swim in.
options.why: Orangutans live in the trees. They do not swim in the sea.
Rainforests are full of many kinds of animals.

options.text: The trees give them food and shelter.

hints: Think about what every habitat gives an animal.
Orangutans eat fruit and sleep in nests high up.
Ask: where do they find fruit and build their nests?
items.explanation: The rainforest trees give orangutans fruit to eat and branches to build nests for sleeping. The forest is their habitat.

items.prompt: Draw a pond habitat. Show and label three living things.

criteria.label: Draws the water and plants of a pond
Draws three living things that live in or near a pond

hints: Frogs, fish, ducks and water plants live in or near ponds.
Add plants at the edge and in the water.
items.explanation: A pond is a habitat. Fish, frogs, ducks, snails and water plants find food, water and shelter there.

items.prompt: Choose the three things a habitat gives an animal.

options.why: Wild animals do not need toys.
Animals do not use money.

hints: Think about what an animal needs to stay alive.
Animals need to eat, drink and stay safe.
Start with food. Does every animal need it?
items.explanation: A habitat gives an animal food, water and shelter, a safe place to rest and raise its young.

items.prompt: A pond has fish, frogs and ducks. Water plants grow in the pond. The plants give the fish food and a place to hide.
hints: Read the first sentence for the animals.
The last sentence tells what the plants give.
A habitat is where an animal lives.
items.explanation: Fish live in the water all their life. The water plants give them food and a place to hide.

parts.prompt: Which animal lives in the water all its life?
What do the water plants give the fish?

options.text: food and a place to hide

items.prompt: Tap the animal that lives in the desert.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: camel, penguin, fish and whale.

hints: A desert is very hot and dry.
This animal can go for days without water.
items.explanation: A camel is well suited to the desert. It can go a long time without water.

items.prompt: Put each animal label on its home.
hints: Think about where each animal can live.
A frog needs water. A camel lives in a hot dry place.
A penguin lives where it is very cold.
items.explanation: A frog lives by a pond, a camel in the desert and a penguin in the cold Arctic.

items.prompt: Which animal lives in the sea?

options.why: A camel lives in the desert.
An owl lives in trees.
A monkey lives in a forest.

items.explanation: A whale lives in the sea.

items.prompt: Where does a crab hide on the seashore?

options.why: Crabs cannot climb trees.
Crabs live by the sea.
Crabs cannot fly.

items.explanation: Crabs hide under rocks and in rock pools on the seashore.

items.prompt: Where would you find a woodlouse?

options.why: Nothing lives there.

options.text: in the middle of a road
options.why: It would be crushed.
It cannot fly.

items.explanation: Woodlice like to live in dark, damp places like under logs.

items.prompt: Why do many woodlice live under stones?

options.text: It is hot and dry there.
options.why: Woodlice like damp places.

options.text: It is dark and damp there.

options.why: Stones are quiet.
Under stones is dark.

items.explanation: Woodlice need damp, dark places. Stones keep them cool and moist.

items.prompt: What does a bird's nest give a baby bird?

options.why: Birds in nests do not swim.
The parents bring food.

options.text: a place to sleep in the sea
options.why: Nests are in trees or bushes.

items.explanation: A nest keeps baby birds safe and warm.

items.prompt: A polar bear's fur is white. How does this help it?

options.why: Colour does not change weight.
Colour does not change speed.
Colour does not do that.

options.text: It hides the bear in the snow.

items.explanation: White fur is camouflage. The bear is hard to see on snow and ice.

items.prompt: A green stick insect sits on a green leaf. Why is it hard to see?

options.why: Size is not the reason.
Sleeping does not hide it.
A noise would give it away.

items.explanation: The insect is camouflaged. It looks like the leaf, so hunters do not see it.

items.prompt: Which habitat gets the least rain?

options.why: A rainforest is very wet.
A pond is full of water.
A river bank is wet.

items.explanation: A desert is very dry and gets very little rain.

items.prompt: Frogs live near ponds. What does a pond give a frog?

options.why: A pond is not icy.
A pond has water and plants.
Frogs do not fly.

items.explanation: A pond gives frogs water for eggs. It gives them insects to eat and plants to hide in.

items.prompt: What happens if a pond dries up?

options.text: The fish and frogs must find a new home or die.

options.why: The animals lose their home.

options.text: More fish are born in the mud.
options.why: There is no water for fish.

options.text: The frogs turn into fish to survive.
options.why: Frogs cannot become fish.

items.explanation: A pond is a habitat. Without water, the animals lose their food, water and shelter.

items.prompt: Is it a hot place or a cold place? Sort the animals.
items.explanation: Camels, desert lizards and scorpions live in hot deserts. Polar bears, penguins and Arctic foxes live in cold places.

items.prompt: Where does it live? Sort the animals.
items.explanation: Ducks and frogs live at ponds. Owls and squirrels live in woodland. Crabs and seagulls live by the sea.

items.prompt: Choose all the living things found in a pond.
items.explanation: A frog, a duck and a water lily live at a pond. A camel and a cactus live in the desert.

items.prompt: Choose all the animals found in a rainforest.
items.explanation: Orangutans, parrots and tigers live in rainforests. Penguins live in icy places and camels live in deserts.

items.prompt: Match each living thing to how it is suited to its habitat.
pairs: big eyes to see at night
items.explanation: A polar bear has thick fur to keep warm. A fish has gills to breathe. An owl has big eyes to see in the dark. A cactus stores water in its stem.

items.prompt: A ___ is a place where a living thing lives. A pond is a ___ habitat.
hints: It is a kind of home.
A pond is full of water.
items.explanation: A habitat is where a living thing lives. A pond is a water habitat.

items.prompt: Where does the animal live?
head: Animal
Habitat
items.explanation: A camel lives in the desert and a frog lives at a pond. A monkey lives in a rainforest and a polar bear lives in the Arctic.

items.prompt: Bayu lifts a log in his garden. It is damp and dark under the log. He sees a woodlouse, a worm and a centipede. They hurry to hide.

parts.prompt: Why do the minibeasts live under the log?

options.text: It is damp, dark and safe.

parts.prompt: How many kinds of minibeast does Bayu see?

hints: Count the animals in the third sentence.
items.explanation: The log gives shelter that is damp and dark. Bayu sees a woodlouse, a worm and a centipede.

items.prompt: A pond has 4 frogs, 3 ducks and 5 fish. How many animals is that?
hints: Add them one at a time.
items.explanation: 4 + 3 + 5 = 12 animals.

items.prompt: Tap the animal that lives in the Arctic.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: polar bear, camel, monkey and snake.

items.explanation: The polar bear lives in the cold Arctic.

items.prompt: Tap the two animals that live in water.

figure.alt: 4 pictures: fish, whale, cat and camel.

items.explanation: Fish and whales live in water. Cats and camels live on land.

items.prompt: Label the habitats. One label is not needed.

figure.alt: Pictures of a pond, a desert and a forest.

items.explanation: The three pictures show a pond, a desert and a forest.

items.prompt: A habitat gives an animal food, water and ___.
items.explanation: A habitat gives an animal food, water and shelter.

items.prompt: Draw a desert habitat with one animal and one plant.

criteria.label: Draws one animal that lives in a desert

hints: A camel or a lizard lives in the desert.
A cactus is a desert plant.
items.explanation: A desert is dry and sandy. Camels, lizards and cactuses live there.

items.prompt: I have thick fur and big paws. I live on the ice and swim well. What am I?

options.why: A camel lives in the desert.
A lion lives in warm grassland.
A parrot lives in warm forests.

hints: It lives where it is icy.
items.explanation: A polar bear has thick fur and big paws. It swims well and lives in the Arctic.

items.prompt: Which animal would not survive in a hot desert?

options.why: Camels live in deserts.
Lizards live in deserts.
Scorpions live in deserts.

hints: Which one lives in the cold?
items.explanation: A polar bear has thick fur for the cold. It would be too hot in a desert.

items.prompt: A pond has 3 ducks, 2 frogs and 4 fish. How many can live out of the water for a while?
hints: Fish need water all the time.
items.explanation: Ducks and frogs can live on land for a while, but fish cannot. 3 + 2 = 5.
